sap-upload: The oil company statement (SAP) is uploaded the same way as a bank statement.
Download your account statement from the oil company portal as an Excel file.
Open Daily Operations, then Upload Transactions.
Step 1: choose the account this statement belongs to.
Then choose the statement file (Excel or PDF).
Step 2: PetroMath reads every line of the statement.
Lines already uploaded before are marked as duplicates and skipped.
Choose a ledger for each line: who paid, or what the money was for.
The ledger list shows only what is allowed for this account.
Product invoices go to Purchase Invoice.
Next time, PetroMath suggests the ledger from what you chose before.
When every line has a ledger, click Next.
Step 3: check the count and the account, then Save All Transactions.
The lines are now in SAP Transactions.
From here they are used for reconciliation and the accounts.
shift-closing: This is the Cashier Shift screen. Every shift is listed here.
In PetroMath, a shift is one cashier's duty: from taking the opening cash to handing over the cash. One 24-hour duty is one shift a day; if cashiers change, enter one shift per cashier.
To start a new shift, click Add New.
The shift has a tab for each part. Start with Closing.
Choose the cashier for this shift.
The date is today. You can pick an earlier day if needed.
Enter the opening cash given to the cashier.
Today's selling rates are filled in from the last shift. Check them.
Click Next. PetroMath saves the shift as a draft.
Attendance: add everyone who worked this shift.
Choose the shift, then the in and out time.
Click Add for each person.
Reading: first choose the time the meter readings were taken.
Click Add All Nozzles. Opening readings come from the last shift.
Type the closing meter reading of each nozzle.
Sale (litres) and Amount work themselves out.
Enter testing litres, if any, so they are not counted as sale.
Lube Sales: oils and other products sold for cash.
Pick the product and enter the quantity. The price comes from the product list.
Credit Sales: one entry for each credit bill.
Enter the product, bill number, company and vehicle.
Enter the quantity in litres. The amount is calculated.
The bill is added to the list. Add the next bill the same way.
Digital Sales: UPI, card and fleet card payments.
The total is shown below the list.
Collections and Employee Advance are optional tabs: you see them only if they are switched on for your station.
Collections: payments from credit customers received during the shift.
Cash or digital, the customer and the amount.
It is added to the shift's cash, and the customer's balance comes down.
Employee Advance: cash given to staff from the shift: salary advance or salary paid.
It is taken out of the shift's cash and goes to the employee's ledger.
Expenses: money paid out of the cash during the shift.
The usual amount is filled in. Change it if needed.
Cash Count: count the cash being handed over.
Enter how many of each note and coin.
The total is worked out for you.
Summary: the whole shift on one page. Check it before closing.
Excess / Shortage compares the cash counted with what was due.
Sales, credit, digital, expenses and cash, all in one place.
When everything is right, click CLOSE.
Confirm with OK. A closed shift can no longer be edited.
Done. The shift is listed as Closed, with its shortage or excess.
Its closing readings become the next shift's opening readings.
PetroMath: every shift, accounted for.
intro: Welcome to PetroMath. A quick tour for the owner of the station.
Open your browser and type petromath.co.in.
This is the PetroMath website. Click Sign in at the top right.
Sign in with the username and password PetroMath gave you.
Click Login.
You land on Cashier Shift: every shift, with its sales and shortage or excess.
Your name and station are at the top left. Everything else is in this menu.
Daily Operations: the work of every day.
Cashier Shift: enter and close each shift.
Day Bill: the GST bill for the day's cash and digital sales.
Day Close: cash in hand, deposits and expenses for the day.
Day-Close Report: the whole day on one page.
Upload Transactions: your bank and oil company statements.
Bank and SAP Transactions: the uploaded lines.
Transactions: money and stock that come in.
Credit Receipts: payments from credit customers.
Purchase Invoice: fuel and lube invoices, straight from the PDF.
Tank Receipts: each tanker load into your tanks.
Tank Dip Entry: the daily dip readings.
Deadlines & Renewals: licences, stamping and other due dates.
Reports.
Customer Balances: who owes you how much.
Customer Detailed Report: a customer's full statement.
Digital Reconciliation: Paytm, card and fleet card money received.
Bank Reconciliation: your books against the bank.
GST Summary and GST Returns: ready for filing.
Stock Summary and Stock Ledger: product stock.
Masters: your set-up. Done once, changed when needed.
Users: logins for your managers and staff.
Products: fuels, lubes and prices.
Customers: credit customers, their vehicles and logins.
Digital: Paytm, card and fleet card.
Bank Master: your bank accounts.
Employees: staff and their salary.
Accounting: your books, written from your daily work.
GL Control: create the accounts each month.
Day Book and Ledger Report: every entry.
Trial Balance.
Profit & Loss: your profit for any month.
Balance Sheet.
Health Check: finds entries that need attention.
Administration.
Support Tickets: raise a question or problem with the PetroMath team.
Password Reset: reset a staff member's password.
Stuck? Click Help at the top for step-by-step videos like this one.
PetroMath: your whole station, in one place.
phone-app: PetroMath works on your phone too, and installs like an app.
Open Chrome on your phone and type petromath.co.in.
Tap Sign in.
Sign in with your username and password.
PetroMath can sign you in with your fingerprint next time. Turn it on now, or later.
Now install the app. Tap Install on the "Get the PetroMath app" banner.
Chrome asks to confirm. Tap Install.
PetroMath is now on your home screen, like any other app.
Tap it to open.
The app opens full screen, already signed in.
Your name and station are at the top.
Every screen is a tile, grouped like the menu on a computer.
Tap "more" to see the rest of a section.
Transactions.
Reports.
Masters.
Accounting.
Or search for any screen by name.
Tap a tile to open it.
PetroMath: your station, in your pocket.
bank-upload: Upload your bank statement to bring every bank credit and debit into PetroMath.
First download the statement from your internet banking as an Excel file.
Open Daily Operations, then Upload Transactions.
Step 1: choose the account this statement belongs to.
Then choose the statement file (Excel or PDF).
Step 2: PetroMath reads every line of the statement.
Lines already uploaded before are marked as duplicates and skipped.
Choose a ledger for each line: who paid, or what the money was for.
The ledger list shows only what is allowed for this account.
A payment to IOCL goes to your SAP account.
Next time, PetroMath suggests the ledger from what you chose before.
When every line has a ledger, click Next.
Step 3: check the count and the account, then Save All Transactions.
The lines are now in Bank Transactions.
From here they are used for reconciliation and the accounts.
customer-statement: The Customer Detailed Report is a credit customer's statement: every bill and payment.
Open Reports, then Customer Detailed Report.
Choose the period. Here, last month.
You can also pick This Month, a month and year, a financial year, or your own dates.
The Period Summary: opening balance, bills, payments and closing balance.
Below it, every bill: date, bill number, product, vehicle, quantity and amount.
Payments appear as credits, and the balance runs line by line.
The statement ends with the totals and the closing balance.
To send it to the customer, click the green Download PDF button.
The PDF has your station name and address at the top.
Share it on WhatsApp or print it. The blue Print button opens it ready to print.
PetroMath: every customer, every bill, accounted for.
customer-phone: Your credit customers can see their own statement on their phone.
They open petromath.co.in and sign in with the username and password you sent them.
Their statement opens straight away, for the last few weeks.
It starts with the opening balance.
Every bill: date, bill number, product, litres and vehicle, with the balance after it.
Payments show in green and bring the balance down.
At the end, the closing balance: what they owe you today.
They can pick another period, for example last month, and tap Go.
The green button downloads the statement as a PDF.
Your station name on top, every bill and payment below.
They can keep it, or forward it to their accounts person.
From the menu they can change their password.
No more calls asking "how much do I owe?"
paytm-recon: Every day cashiers enter Paytm collections in the shift, and Paytm pays them into your bank.
Reconciliation checks that every rupee collected was paid to you.
Open Reports, then Digital Reconciliation.
Choose the period and the digital vendor: here, last month and PAYTM.
Click Go.
Debits are the Paytm sales from your shifts. Credits are Paytm payments into your bank.
PetroMath matches them for you: each day's sales with the next day's payment.
Lines with the same Match ID belong together.
Tick Show Only Unreconciled to see what is left.
Two days were paid together in one payment, so they could not match one-to-one.
Select the two sales and the payment.
The difference is zero.
Click Manual Match.
Matched.
One payment came ₹47 short of the sale.
Select the sale and the payment.
Click Manual Match.
A difference needs a note: say why it is short.
Click Save & Match.
Saved, with your note.
Nothing left to reconcile for the month.
Your manual matches keep their Match ID. The red ✕ next to it unmatches a group.
Do this every month, for every digital vendor.
add-customer: Adding a credit customer: their details, what they owed from your old books, and a login.
Customers are added by the owner (Admin). Open Masters, then Customers.
Every customer is listed with their opening balance and login.
Click Add Customer.
Enter the company name, a short name for bills, and the phone number.
The address, and the GST number if they need tax invoices.
Remittance Bank: the account they pay into.
Their payments then appear under this customer when you upload that bank statement.
Opening Balance: what they owed before their first bill in PetroMath.
"As on" is filled in: the day before you started on PetroMath.
Enter the amount from your old ledger. Leave 0 for a brand-new customer.
Click Save Customer.
Saved.
Search for the customer.
The opening balance is set, as on that date.
PetroMath also made a login, so the customer can see their own bills and statement.
To see the login details, click the key.
The username, and the password (hidden in this video).
Copy them and send them to the customer, for example on WhatsApp.
Reset Password gives a new one if they forget it. You can also switch the login off here.
Add their vehicles with the truck button. They're ready for credit bills.
add-product: Adding a product you sell: lubes, coolant, or any other item.
Every product is listed with its unit, price and opening stock.
Enter the product name as you want it on bills, with the pack size.
The HSN code from the supplier invoice.
The unit: NOS for packs and bottles, LIT for loose oil.
The GST rate: half as CGST, half as SGST. 18% is 9 and 9.
Non-Fuel Product is ticked, so PetroMath tracks its stock.
The product is added. Cashiers can now pick it in Lube Sales and Credit Sales.
Its opening stock is not set yet. Click Set.
Opening stock: how many you have in hand when you start selling it in PetroMath.
Enter the quantity from a physical count.
Opening stock is set. Purchases add to it, and every sale takes from it.
To change a price later, use the edit button on the product.
fuel-invoice: When a tanker arrives, enter the oil company's invoice from its PDF. No typing.
Click New Purchase, then Fuel Invoice.
Click Choose File and pick the invoice PDF you downloaded.
Your Downloads folder: select the invoice PDF and click Open.
Everything is filled in from the PDF: invoice number, date, tanker number and total.
And each product: quantity, rate, density and HSN code, with the VAT charges below.
The first time only, tell PetroMath which of your products each invoice product is.
PetroMath remembers this, so next time it is picked for you.
Check the figures against the paper invoice, then click Save Mapping.
Saved. The PDF is kept with the invoice, so you can open it any time.
Purchases, stock and accounts now include this tanker.
lube-invoice: Lube purchases are entered the same way: from the distributor's invoice PDF.
Click New Purchase, then Lube Invoice.
Select the invoice PDF and click Open.
The supplier, invoice number and date are filled in.
Every product line too: quantity, rate, discount and GST.
Each line is linked to your product: Matched. Check any marked Suggested or Pick.
Here is the invoice PDF. Private details are blurred in this video.
Same products, quantities and amounts as the screen.
The figures from the PDF are locked, so they match the invoice exactly.
The total matches the invoice total.
When it is right, click Save & Close Invoice.
Saved. The stock of each product goes up, and the invoice PDF is attached.
accounting: PetroMath writes your accounts from your daily work: shifts, bills, invoices and bank lines.
Each month, the owner (Admin) runs two steps. Open Accounting, then GL Control.
Step 1: Generate Events.
Choose the month. Here, January 2026.
Click Generate Missing Events.
Every sale, receipt, invoice and bank line of the month is queued for the accounts.
Events Monitor shows the queue.
All of them are waiting (Unprocessed).
The eye button shows the transaction behind any event.
Step 2: Create Accounting.
Click Run Create Accounting.
Done: the vouchers are written. Dates with a shift still in draft are skipped until it is closed.
Now open Profit & Loss.
Choose January 2026 and click View.
Total income, total expenses, and the net profit for the month.
Income: fuel and lube sales, and the dealer margin.
Expenses: purchases, then salary, rent, bank charges and other costs.
Purchases are adjusted for stock: opening + purchases − closing, so you see what was actually sold.
Every ledger opens to the entries behind it. Click OTHERS.
The Ledger Report: each entry with its date, voucher and description.
Here: two stamping fee payments from the bank statement.
If an entry looks wrong, correct the tag on that bank line and run Create Accounting again.
Back to the Profit & Loss. Now GENERAL EXPENSES.
The day-to-day cash spends entered in the shift closing, each with its note.
So every figure in your Profit & Loss can be checked, line by line.
PetroMath: your books, straight from your daily work.
day-close: Day Close: once a day, after all of the day's shifts are closed, the cash for the whole day is closed.
Open Daily Operations, then Day Close.
Each day you pick the date and click Generate Day Close. PetroMath brings in the day's shifts.
Here 09-Nov is already generated (Draft). Click Continue Day Close.
At the top: the day's closed shifts, and the cash each cashier handed over.
InFlow: yesterday's cash balance (Balance B/F), the shift collections, 2T oil and cashier excess.
OutFlow: cashier shortage and the expenses entered in the shifts. PetroMath fills all of these in.
Add what PetroMath cannot know. Here: the cash deposited in the bank. Click +.
The Difference is the cash that should be in your cash box now.
Count the notes and enter how many of each. Here they were counted already: 33 rupees short.
Click SAVE, then CLOSE.
Confirm with OK. A closed day can no longer be changed.
Closing the day opens its Day-Close Report: the whole day's business on one page.
It is ready for any day: pick the date and click Go. The green button downloads it as a PDF to share.
Sales in litres for each product: meter flow, testing, credit sales and the rest (cash and digital).
Sales in rupees: how much came as cash, digital and credit, and the total.
Lubes and other items sold.
Digital sales: Paytm, card and fleet card.
Every credit bill of the day.
The day's expenses.
Each cashier shift: litres sold of each product, and its excess or shortage.
Tanker loads received, with the invoice number and amount.
Payments received from credit customers.
Credit customer balances: the top 3 customers who owe you the most, with the notional interest at 12% for the day.
The last row, Total, is the balance of ALL your credit customers together: your money in the market.
On the 15th and on the last day of the month, every customer with a balance is listed.
The day's selling prices.
Fuel bought (offtake) in kilolitres: this month, last month and the same month last year.
Opening and closing meter readings of every nozzle, testing and sale.
The Day Close you just closed: cash in and cash out.
The cash balance against the notes counted: the day's cash excess or shortage.
The day's bank and oil company (SAP) statement lines, once uploaded.
And what is due: renewals, rent and other deadlines.
A snapshot of the whole day. Read it every morning.
PetroMath: every day, closed and accounted for.
add-user: Everyone who uses PetroMath gets their own login. What they can see depends on their role.
Admin is the owner's role. PetroMath gives the owner this login.
Manager: for the person who runs the station day to day.
Cashier: for your cashiers and pump attendants.
Each role has its own default menu and access.
Want a role to see more, or less, at your station? Ask PetroMath, and we add or remove that access for the role.
Open Masters, then Users.
Everyone at your station is listed, with their role.
Click Add User.
Type the full name, in capital letters.
The username is made for you, from the name and your station code.
Every new login starts with the password shown here. Ask them to change it after they sign in.
Choose the role. Here, Manager.
Click Save.
Saved.
An attendant is added the same way, with the Cashier role.
Cashiers and attendants show up in each shift's Attendance, so you can mark who worked.
When someone leaves, click Disable. They can no longer sign in, and their past entries stay.
Confirm with OK.
Disabled users are kept under Disabled. Enable brings them back.
If someone forgets their password, reset it from Administration, then Password Reset.
PetroMath: the right access for every person.
